# Awesome Agent Trace & Evidence Attribution [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re) [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2606.04990-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04990) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [![PRs Welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg)](http://makeapullrequest.com) **Agents are judged by their final answers — but trust lives in the trace.** Which evidence supported each claim? Where did a tool argument come from? Which step, agent, or memory item caused the failure? This list maps research on **evidence tracing**, **execution provenance**, and **failure attribution** — methods, benchmarks, and tools that record, represent, attribute, enforce, debug, and learn from **LLM-agent traces**. **30+ taxonomies & attribution methods | 20+ safety & memory-provenance papers | 25+ benchmarks & datasets | 15+ observability tools & standards | Continuously updated** This repository accompanies the survey: > **From Agent Traces to Trust: A Survey of Evidence Tracing and Execution Provenance in LLM Agents** > > Yiqi Wang, Jiaqi Zhang, Zhangkai Wu, Taotao Cai, Zirui Liu, Qingqiang Sun, Zequn Sun, Manqing Dong, Mingkai Zheng, Xuefei Yin, Yanming Zhu > > [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04990) --- ## Contents - [Contributing](#contributing) - [Citation](#citation) - [License](#license) --- ## Why Agent Traces? LLM agents plan, retrieve, call tools, write memory, act in environments, and talk to each other — yet they are still evaluated almost entirely by final answers. A correct answer reveals nothing about *how* the output was produced, and a failed run gives no pointer to *which* step decided the outcome. Agent traces (recorded artifacts of an agent run: instructions, retrievals, tool calls and outputs, memory operations, observations, intermediate claims, inter-agent messages, actions) are the substrate for closing this **process-level accountability gap**. Two lenses organize the field: - **Execution provenance** — the full typed graph of an agent execution: evidence units, execution units, and relations such as `SUPPORT`, `CONTRADICT`, `DEPEND-ON`, `DERIVE`, `TRIGGER`, `UPDATE`, `INVALIDATE`. - **Evidence tracing** — the projection of that graph onto evidence-support relations: which evidence backs which claim, decision, or action.

Framework overview: a heterogeneous agent execution (reasoning, retrieval, tools, memory, environment, multi-agent) is recorded as a provenance layer of typed evidence/execution units and relations, which feeds downstream trust functions — verification, attribution, debugging, safety, audit, and recovery. (Figure from the companion survey.)

The six-dimension taxonomy of agent provenance: trace sources, evidence and execution units, provenance relations, tracing granularity and timing, representation forms, and trust functions. (Figure from the companion survey.)

How this awesome list maps onto the pipeline: trace sources → trace representation → trace understanding (attribution, diagnosis, debugging) → trace-governed execution (safety, memory, learning) → trust functions (verification, audit, recovery).

--- ## Surveys & Overviews 1. **From Agent Traces to Trust: A Survey of Evidence Tracing and Execution Provenance in LLM Agents** (2026) *Yiqi Wang, Jiaqi Zhang, Zhangkai Wu, Taotao Cai, Zirui Liu, Qingqiang Sun, Zequn Sun, Manqing Dong, Mingkai Zheng, Xuefei Yin, Yanming Zhu* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04990) -- The companion survey of this list: a six-dimension taxonomy (trace sources, evidence/execution units, relations, granularity & timing, representation, trust functions) and seven research threads from provenance representation to failure diagnosis. 2. **A Survey for LLM Agent Trajectory Analysis: From Failure Attribution to Enhancement** (TSE 2026) *Junjie Wang, Mengzhuo Chen, et al.* [[Paper]](https://www.computer.org/csdl/journal/ts/5555/01/11626967/2iuF5rxPMqs) [[GitHub]](https://github.com/IcyFeather233/Awesome-LLM-Agent-Trajectory-Analysis) -- Systematic review of trajectory analysis: failure taxonomy, attribution, system enhancement, monitoring tools, and datasets; ships a 4,316-trajectory annotated dataset. 3. **Survey on Evaluation of LLM-based Agents** (ACL 2025 Findings) *Bing Wang, Xinyi Dai, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16416) -- Broad evaluation landscape for LLM agents, including process- and trajectory-level evaluation perspectives. 4. **Attribution, Citation, and Quotation: A Survey of Evidence-Based Text Generation with LLMs** (2025) *Tobias Schreieder, Tim Schopf, Michael Färber* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.15396) -- Survey of evidence-based generation: attribution, citation, and quotation across the grounding literature. 5. **From Reasoning to Agentic: Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning for LLMs** (2026) *Chenchen Zhang* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.09459) [[GitHub]](https://github.com/xxzcc/Awesome-Credit-Assignment-in-LLM-RL) -- 47-method survey of credit assignment across token/step/turn/multi-agent granularities; the training-side mirror of failure attribution. 6. **A Survey of Process Reward Models** (2025) *Fei Du, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08049) -- Step-level reward models that judge trajectory prefixes, from math reasoning to agentic tasks. 7. **A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of Large Language Model Based Agents** (ACM TOIS 2025) *Zeyu Zhang, Xiaohe Bo, Chen Ma, Rui Li, Xu Chen, Quanyu Dai, Jieming Zhu, Zhenhua Dong, Ji-Rong Wen* [[Paper]](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3748302) -- What agents store, how memories are written/read/updated — the substrate memory provenance builds on. 8. **Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Emerging Frontiers** (2026) *Pengfei Du* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.07670) -- Mechanisms and evaluation protocols for agent memory. 9. **Graph-Based Agent Memory: Taxonomy, Techniques, and Applications** (2026) *Chang Yang, Chuang Zhou, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05665) -- Relational/graph memory systems for agents. --- ## Foundations: Standards, Schemas & Provenance Models 10. **W3C PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model** (W3C Recommendation, 2013) [[Spec]](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/) -- Entities, activities, agents and derivation/usage/invalidation relations — the base vocabulary agent provenance extends with `SUPPORT`/`CONTRADICT` and trust labels. 11. **OpenTelemetry — GenAI & Agents Semantic Conventions** (2026) [[Spec]](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) -- Spans for LLM calls, tool invocations, and agent execution; the de-facto runtime trace interchange for agent observability stacks. 12. **OpenLineage Specification** (2026) [[Spec]](https://github.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage/blob/main/spec/OpenLineage.md) -- Lineage standard for data workflows; a reference point for cross-system agent provenance. 13. **PROV-AGENT: Unified Provenance for Tracking AI Agent Interactions in Agentic Workflows** (IEEE eScience 2025) *Renan Souza, Amal Gueroudji, Stephen DeWitt, et al.* IEEE eScience 2025 -- Adapts PROV modeling to agentic workflows: prompts, decisions, tool interactions, and workflow context. 14. **AgentTrace: A Structured Logging Framework for Agent System Observability** (2026) *Adam AlSayyad, Kelvin Yuxiang Huang, Richik Pal* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10133) -- Organizes execution records into operational, cognitive, and contextual logs. 15. **AgentOps: Enabling Observability of LLM Agents** (2024) *Liming Dong, Qinghua Lu, Liming Zhu* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05285) [[Code]](https://github.com/AgentOps-AI/agentops) -- Observability architecture that records agent artifacts and their lifecycle relationships. 16. **OpenInference** (Arize AI) [[Spec]](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference) -- Open instrumentation convention for LLM/agent tracing, natively emitted through OpenTelemetry. ### Agent Substrates (Trace Sources) 17. **ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models** (ICLR 2023) *Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629) -- The reasoning–action loop whose thought/action/observation records became the canonical agent trace format. 18. **Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools** (NeurIPS 2023) *Timo Schick, Jane Dwivedi-Yu, Roberto Dessì, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761) -- Self-supervised API-call insertion; the earliest tool-call trace construction at scale. 19. **ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs** (ICLR 2024) *Yujia Qin, Shihao Liang, Yining Ye, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.16789) [[Code]](https://github.com/OpenBMB/ToolBench) -- ToolBench trajectories: API-call paths with arguments, outputs, and failures. 20. **AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation** (COLM 2024) *Qingyun Wu, Gagan Bansal, Jieyu Zhang, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155) [[Code]](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen) -- Multi-agent conversation framework; message logs as a trace source. 21. **CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society** (NeurIPS 2023) *Guohao Li, Hasan Hammoud, Hani Itani, Dmitrii Khizbullin, Bernard Ghanem* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17760) [[Code]](https://github.com/camel-ai/camel) -- Role-playing multi-agent trajectories via inception prompting. 22. **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** (Anthropic, 2024) [[Spec]](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol) -- Standardized tool/server interface that defines the execution boundary MCP-safety and tool-provenance work targets. --- ## Observability Platforms & Trace Tooling ### Open-Source Platforms 23. **Langfuse** — open-source LLM engineering platform; OpenTelemetry-native traces, prompt management, evaluations, and agent session replay. [[GitHub]](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse) 24. **Arize Phoenix** — LLM/agent tracing, evals, and experimentation built on OpenInference; datasets + playground for trace-level debugging. [[GitHub]](https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix) 25. **AgentOps (SDK)** — drop-in agent observability SDK: session recording, tool-call timelines, replay, and failure analytics. [[GitHub]](https://github.com/AgentOps-AI/agentops) 26. **MLflow Tracing** — GenAI/agent tracing in MLflow (OpenAI/LangGraph autologging), trace-level evaluation. [[GitHub]](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow) [[Docs]](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/llms/tracing/) 27. **W&B Weave** — trace, evaluate, and iterate on LLM apps and agents inside Weights & Biases. [[GitHub]](https://github.com/wandb/weave) 28. **OpenLIT** — OpenTelemetry-native LLM & agent monitoring (metrics + traces) in a single binary. [[GitHub]](https://github.com/openlit/openlit) 29. **OpenLLMetry (Traceloop)** — OTel SDKs instrumenting LLM providers, vector DBs, and agent frameworks. [[GitHub]](https://github.com/traceloop/openllmetry) 30. **LangSmith & LangGraph** — commercial tracing/eval platform; LangGraph persists step-level graph state with checkpointing and time-travel replay. [[Website]](https://www.langchain.com/langsmith) [[Code]](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph) 31. **Helicone** — open-source LLM proxy for logging, caching, and observability. [[GitHub]](https://github.com/Helicone/helicone) ### Research Tooling & Debuggers 32. **AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18754) -- Unified event representation (on OTel GenAI spans) with a 19-pattern seed vocabulary; observability → attribution → recovery loop in one toolkit. 33. **MAESTRO: Multi-Agent Evaluation Suite for Testing, Reliability, and Observability** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00481) [[Code]](https://github.com/sands-lab/maestro) -- Testing/reliability/observability suite for multi-agent systems. 34. **Signals: Trajectory Sampling and Triage for Agentic Interactions** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.00356) -- Sampling and triage of agent trajectories for human review. 35. **DiLLS: Interactive Diagnosis of LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems via Layered Summary of Agent Behaviors** (CHI 2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05446) -- Layered behavioral summaries for interactive MAS diagnosis. 36. **XAgen: An Explainability Tool for Identifying and Correcting Failures in Multi-Agent Workflows** (CHI 2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17896) -- Human-in-the-loop explainability and correction for multi-agent failures. 37. **LADYBUG: An LLM Agent Debugger for Data-Driven Applications** (EDBT 2025) *Joel Rorseth, Parke Godfrey, Lukasz Golab, Divesh Srivastava, Jarek Szlichta* [[Paper]](https://openproceedings.org/2025/conf/edbt/paper-313.pdf) -- Trace-based debugging to support failure localization and repair. 38. **Trajectory Guard: A Lightweight, Sequence-Aware Model for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Agentic AI** (AAAI Workshop 2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00516) -- Real-time trajectory anomaly detection over streaming agent actions. 39. **Taming Uncertainty via Automation: Observing, Analyzing, and Optimizing Agentic AI Systems** (2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.11277) -- End-to-end observe–analyze–optimize loop over agent execution. 40. **AgentEval: DAG-Structured Step-Level Evaluation for Agentic Workflows with Error Propagation Tracking** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23581) -- DAG evaluation structure that tracks how errors propagate across workflow steps. 41. **ProMAS: Proactive Error Forecasting for Multi-Agent Systems Using Markov Transition Dynamics** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20260) -- Forecasting errors before they surface from transition dynamics over trace states. --- ## Evidence Attribution & Grounding 42. **FEVER: A Large-Scale Dataset for Fact Extraction and Verification** (NAACL 2018) *James Thorne, Andreas Vlachos, Christos Christodoulopoulos, Arpit Mittal* [[Paper]](https://aclanthology.org/N18-1074/) -- The foundational claim-evidence support/REFUTES/NEI annotation scheme. 43. **Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations (ALCE)** (EMNLP 2023) *Tianyu Gao, Howard Yen, Jiatong Yu, Danqi Chen* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14627) [[Code]](https://github.com/princeton-nlp/ALCE) -- Citation generation and citation-quality evaluation for long-form outputs. 44. **FActScore: Fine-Grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation** (EMNLP 2023) *Sewon Min, Kalpesh Krishna, Xinxi Lyu, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14251) -- Decomposes outputs into atomic facts and scores support — claim-level granularity for tracing. 45. **How Well Do LLMs Cite Relevant Medical References? (SourceCheckup)** (2024) *Kevin Wu, Eric Wu, Ally Cassasola, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02008) -- Shows a cited source can be *relevant without supporting* the claim — the citation ≠ support distinction. 46. **RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models** (ACL 2024) *Cheng Niu, Yuanhao Wu, Juno Zhu, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.00396) -- Word/span-level hallucination labels over RAG outputs. 47. **RAGChecker: A Fine-Grained Framework for Diagnosing Retrieval-Augmented Generation** (NeurIPS 2024) *Dongyu Ru, Lin Qiu, Xiangkun Hu, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.08067) [[Code]](https://github.com/amazon-science/RAGChecker) -- Claim-level claim–evidence graph diagnostics separating retriever vs. generator failures. 48. **RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation** (EACL 2024 Demo) *Shahul Es, Jithin James, Luis Espinosa Anke, Steven Schockaert* [[Paper]](https://aclanthology.org/2024.eacl-demo.16/) [[Code]](https://github.com/explodinggradients/ragas) -- Faithfulness / context-relevance / answer-relevance metrics, widely used for grounding checks. 49. **ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems** (NAACL 2024) *Jon Saad-Falcon, Omar Khattab, Christopher Potts, Matei Zaharia* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09476) [[Code]](https://github.com/stanford-futuredata/ares) -- LLM-judge + confidence-interval evaluation for context relevance and faithfulness. 50. **PaperTrail: A Claim-Evidence Interface for Grounding Provenance in LLM-based Scholarly Q&A** (CHI 2026) *Anna Martin-Boyle, Cara Leckey, Martha Brown, Harmanpreet Kaur* CHI 2026 -- Decomposes answers and sources into discrete claims and evidence units — supported, unsupported, and omitted evidence made inspectable. --- ## Error & Failure Taxonomies 51. **Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)** (2025) *Mert Cemri, Melissa Z. Pan, Shuyi Yang, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13657) [[Code]](https://github.com/multi-agent-systems-failure-taxonomy/MAST) -- 14 failure modes in 3 categories derived from 150 annotated traces (inter-annotator agreement κ = 0.88); failures are systematic, not random. 52. **Where LLM Agents Fail and How They Can Learn From Failures (AgentDebug / AgentErrorTaxonomy)** (2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25370) [[Code]](https://github.com/ulab-uiuc/AgentDebug) -- 17 error types across memory/reflection/planning/action/system modules; ships AgentErrorBench (200 failures). Note: withdrawn from ICLR 2026 by the authors. 53. **Failure Modes in LLM Systems: A System-Level Taxonomy for Reliable AI Applications** (2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.19933) -- 15 "hidden" failure modes beyond the model itself: harness, tools, and infrastructure included. 54. **Model or Harness? An Interaction-Centric Taxonomy for Localizing Agent Failures** (2026) *Raj et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28802) -- 41 patterns on a 6-component interaction graph, each labeled model-side vs. surrounding-stack-side — result labels alone cannot assign the fix. 55. **Aegis: Taxonomy and Optimizations for Overcoming Agent-Environment Failures in LLM Agents** (2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.19504) -- Error taxonomy for agent–environment mismatch plus workflow optimizations. 56. **How Do LLMs Fail in Agentic Scenarios? A Qualitative Analysis of Success and Failure Scenarios** (NeurIPS 2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.07497) -- Qualitative success/failure analysis of LLMs in agentic simulations. 57. **Exploring Autonomous Agents: A Closer Look at Why They Fail When Completing Tasks** (ASE 2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13143) -- Empirical failure study of autonomous agents on real tasks. 58. **Demystifying the Lifecycle of Failures in Platform-Orchestrated Agentic Workflows** (2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23735) -- 307 trajectories annotated over the full failure lifecycle, with repair strategies. 59. **Understanding Software Engineering Agents: A Study of Thought-Action-Result Trajectories** (ASE 2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.18824) -- Large-scale study of SWE-agent TAR trajectories. 60. **Beyond Final Code: A Process-Oriented Error Analysis of Software Development Agents in Real-World GitHub Scenarios** (2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12374) -- Process-level (not diff-level) error analysis of dev agents. --- ## Failure Attribution & Trace Debugging Given a failed trajectory, attribute responsibility — *who* (agent), *when* (step/span/stage), and *why* (error mode) — then repair. ### Multi-Agent Failure Attribution 61. **Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When? (Who&When)** (ICML 2025 Spotlight) *Zhang et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00212) [[Code]](https://github.com/ag2ai/Agents_Failure_Attribution) -- First to formalize failure attribution as an independent, benchmarked task; counterfactual "earliest decisive error step" ground truth. 62. **AgenTracer: Who Is Inducing Failure in the LLM Agentic Systems?** (ICLR 2026) *Guibin Zhang, Junhao Wang, Junjie Chen, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.03312) [[Code]](https://github.com/bingreeky/AgenTracer) -- Trained tracer via counterfactual replay + fault injection (labels determined by construction, zero human annotation). 63. **Aegis: Automated Error Generation and Attribution for Multi-Agent Systems** (2025) *Fanqi Kong, Ruijie Zhang, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.14295) -- Positive–negative trajectory pair construction to identify faulty agents and error modes. 64. **Seeing the Whole Elephant: A Benchmark for Failure Attribution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems (TraceElephant)** (ACL 2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22708) [[Code]](https://github.com/TraceElephant/TraceElephant) -- Role-aware and recoverability-aware attribution principles: blame falls where the error *should have been caught*, not merely where it first appeared; full-decision-context traces raise step-level accuracy by ~76% over output-only. 65. **Where Did It All Go Wrong? A Hierarchical Look into Multi-Agent Error Attribution (ECHO)** (NeurIPS 2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04886) -- Hierarchical (system/agent/step) attribution. 66. **Who Is Introducing the Failure? Automatically Attributing Failures of Multi-Agent Systems via Spectrum Analysis (FAMAS)** (ESEC/FSE 2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.13782) -- Borrows spectrum-based fault localization from software testing into MAS attribution. 67. **Abduct, Act, Predict: Scaffolding Causal Inference for Automated Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems (A2P)** (NeurIPS 2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.10401) [[Code]](https://github.com/ResearAI/A2P) -- Causal-inference scaffolding for attribution. 68. **Automatic Failure Attribution and Critical Step Prediction Based on Causal Inference (CDC-MAS)** (2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08682) -- Causal-discovery-based critical step prediction. 69. **From Flat Logs to Causal Graphs: Hierarchical Failure Attribution for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23701) -- Upgrades flat logs into causal graphs before attribution. 70. **CORRECT: Condensed eRror Recognition via Knowledge Transfer in Multi-Agent Systems** (2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.24088) -- Condensed error recognition with knowledge transfer; ships CORRECT-Error (2,000+ trajectories). 71. **Towards Self-Improving Error Diagnosis in Multi-Agent Systems (ERRORPROBE)** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17658) -- Iterative, self-improving diagnosis loop. 72. **DoVer: Intervention-Driven Auto Debugging for LLM Multi-Agent Systems** (ICLR 2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.06749) [[Website]](https://mbjinx.github.io/DoVer_Web/) -- Interventions on the execution to verify causal hypotheses about failures. 73. **Rethinking Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems: A Multi-Perspective Benchmark and Evaluation (MP-Bench)** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25001) -- Benchmark with failure-reason and ideal-action annotations. 74. **Traceability and Accountability in Role-Specialized Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines** (2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07614) -- Message-level provenance and responsibility in role-specialized pipelines. ### Single-Agent, Span-Level and Domain Diagnosis 75. **TRAIL: Trace Reasoning and Agentic Issue Localization** (2025) *Darshan Deshpande, Varun Gangal, Hersh Mehta, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.08638) [[Code]](https://github.com/patronus-ai/trail-benchmark) -- 148 human-annotated traces with 841 error annotations under a formal issue taxonomy; the best model localizes issues at only ~11% accuracy. 76. **FALAT: Tracing Failures in LLM Agent Trajectories via Dependency-Guided Search** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00765) -- Reframes attribution as search over a hierarchical dependency structure instead of step classification. 77. **Tracing Agentic Failure from the Flow of Success** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12747) -- One-class learning: model normality from successful trajectories instead of enumerating failure modes. 78. **AgentRx: Diagnosing AI Agent Failures from Execution Trajectories** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02475) -- First *unrecoverable failure step* annotation: the step after which no continuation can save the run. 79. **TrajAudit: Automated Failure Diagnosis for Agentic Coding Systems** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26563) -- Stage-level diagnosis for coding agents; The strongest objection to trace analysis: visible reasoning text may be a post-hoc narrative rather than the mechanism. Know the boundary conditions. 152. **LLM Reasoning Is Latent, Not the Chain of Thought** (2026) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15726) -- Position: answers are encoded in latent states before being spoken; CoT is a selective, sometimes unfaithful interface. 153. **Chain-of-Thought Is Not Explainability** (2025) *Fazl Barez, TY Wu, et al. (Oxford)* [[Paper]](https://fbarez.github.io/assets/pdf/Cot_Is_Not_Explainability.pdf) -- Position paper: CoT ≠ explanation, systematically reviewed. 154. **Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in the Wild Is Not Always Faithful** (2025) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08679) -- Empirical faithfulness failures of naturally occurring CoT. 155. **Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet** (ICLR 2024) *Jie Huang, et al.* [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01798) -- Without external feedback, self-correction degrades accuracy — models cannot *find* their reasoning errors. 156. **Judging the Judges: A Systematic Study of Position Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge** (2024) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07791) -- Systematic judge biases; a strong reasoning model is not automatically a reliable trace annotator. > **Working consensus in trace research:** actions, tool calls, and retrieved evidence are externally verifiable events and robust to the faithfulness critique; free-text self-narration is not. Prefer attribution methods anchored in verifiable events and cross-trajectory statistics over single-trace introspection. --- ## Benchmarks & Datasets | Benchmark | Venue / Link | Scale | Annotation
